matt: rolling Vela21B int4 canary (canary=5%) this morning. coldstart runs are hitting OOMs and memory fragmentation spikes on a few hosts, esp when max_new_tokens is high. anyone seen this pattern before?
reza: can you paste the canary config + the exact error logs? is this during first token generation or later in the stream?
matt: logs attached (snip) — errors show `cudaMalloc` failure after ~40s on first request. config: ```model: vela-21b-quant-int4
prefetch_kv: true
prefetch_batch_size: 16
max_new_tokens_default: 512
adaptive_window: on
kv_trim_threshold: 0.6
```. looks like KV cache warmup + prefetch combined with big max_new tokens triggers fragmentation.
june: +1 on fragmentation hypothesis. for other 20b-class int4 onboards we've mitigated by: 1) lowering default max_new_tokens for hosted canary to 128, 2) enabling conservative cwnd pacing (microbatch cwnd=8 -> 4) and 3) bumping kv_trim_frequency during warmup. can we try that as a quick experiment?
samantha: quick quality note — switching to lower max_new_tokens for canary shouldn't affect eval pass rate much (we run short-forms). but we should run the usual eval set (summaries + instruction-following) after we toggle. i can queue evals once you push the change.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for vela-21b-int4 (5%) — job id 670128. monitoring enabled.
matt: proposing immediate delta: set `max_new_tokens_default=128`, `prefetch_batch_size=8`, `microbatch_cwnd=4`, `kv_trim_threshold=0.45`, and add fallback rule for OOM >=3 in 10min -> switch to vela-21b-int8 variant. also enable extra compaction on warmup: `gpu_compact_on_alloc=true`.
reza: sounds sensible. curious if kernel selection is picking a pathological kernel for the longer sequences; can you grab a perf profile with `--kernels-trace` on two failing hosts? that will help tell if we need a kernel blacklist.
june: also recommend temporarily disabling continuous prefetching for hosts showing fragmentation and instead run on-demand prefetch for first 8 tokens (prefetch_limit=8). that reduced fragmentation in a recent 14b rollout.
alec: +1 for fallback to int8 variant. add a metric to the model dashboard that counts OOMs per 1000 requests and auto-aborts canary at threshold 10.
samantha: queuing evals now — I'll run the short generator and the instruction compliance suite after the changes and ping results here. expect 30m run.
matt: ok I'm going to apply the config delta to canary pool only. will keep the 5% traffic. if OOMs drop to zero for 30m and perf looks stable, we can widen. will also attach the `--kernels-trace` logs to this thread once available. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: config update applied to canary pool (job 670129). watchers notified.
matt: update 25m: OOMs reduced from 6->0 in the failing host group after change. initial quality evals show no regression on short-form tasks. keeping watch for 2h.
june: nice. follow-up todo: schedule a kernel blacklist test and try a microbatch pacing anneal to restore throughput without reintroducing frag. file a small runbook for future onboards.
samantha: eval results: BLEU-ish style metric stable, instruction pass rate 98.7% -> 98.6% (noise). no urgent quality regressions.
reza: attaching kernel traces. I see a long tail on one matmul kernel that aligns with the spike right before OOM. will open a patch to prefer alt-kernel for that op.
matt: plan agreed: (1) keep canary config changes, (2) add fallback to int8 at OOM threshold, (3) patch kernel selection and test in canary, (4) create short runbook for warmup frag mitigation. closing thread after 2h of green or earlier if any regression.
ops-bot: monitor-bot: canary metrics (last 30m) — OOMs: 0, avg p95 latency: 312ms, 99.9th: 1.8s, cpu/gpu compaction events: 4.
matt: thanks all — will post the runbook and the kernel patch PR reference once they're up.
